policy_name: New Jersey act against discrimination in automated hiring
question: In layman's terms, what specific actions regarding automated employment decision tools are prohibited under this act?
answer_1:
1. It is unlawful to sell or offer for sale an automated employment decision tool in New Jersey without having conducted a bias audit in the past year prior to the sale, and without including an annual bias audit service at no additional cost. (Section b)
2. Employers using an automated employment decision tool must notify candidates within 30 days if the tool was used in connection with their application for employment, and the tool assessed their job qualifications or characteristics. (Section c)
3. Violations of the provisions of this act can result in civil penalties of up to $1,500 per violation. (Section d)
4. The New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development, in consultation with the Division on Civil Rights, will promulgate rules and regulations to enforce the provisions of this act. (Section f)

Source: P.L.   , c.    (C.        ) (pending before the Legislature as this bill)
answer_2: 1. It is unlawful to sell or offer for sale automated employment decision tools in New Jersey without a bias audit conducted in the past year, an annual bias audit service, and a notice stating the tool is subject to this act. 2. Any person using an automated employment decision tool to screen a candidate for employment must notify the candidate within 30 days that the tool was used and assessed their job qualifications or characteristics. 3. Violations of this act can result in civil penalties ranging from $500 to $1,500 per violation, payable to the State Treasurer.

2. The sale of the tool must include, at no additional cost, an annual bias audit service that provides the results of the audit to the purchaser (P.L.   , c.    (C.        ) (pending before the Legislature as this bill), section b(2)).

answer_2: 1) Companies selling automated employment decision tools must have conducted a bias audit in the past year before selling the tool. 2) The sale of the tool must include an annual bias audit service at no additional cost. 3) Companies using the tools must notify candidates within 30 days if an automated employment decision tool was used in their application process. 4) Violations of the act can result in civil penalties payable to the State Treasurer. 5) The New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development, in consultation with the Division on Civil Rights, may promulgate rules and regulations to enforce the act. policy_name: New Jersey act against discrimination in automated hiring
question: How does this act define 'automated employment decision tool' and what types of systems does this definition encompass?
answer_1: The Act defines an 'automated employment decision tool' as any system the function of which is governed by statistical theory, or systems the parameters of which are defined by systems, including inferential methodologies, linear regression, neural networks, decision trees, random forests, and other learning algorithms, which automatically filters candidates or prospective candidates for hire or for any term, condition or privilege of employment in a way that establishes a preferred candidate or candidates (New Jersey Legislature, P.L.   , c.    (C.        ) (pending before the Legislature as this bill)). This definition encompasses a wide range of systems that use machine learning and artificial intelligence to make decisions about employment, including but not limited to systems based on linear regression, neural networks, decision trees, random forests, and other learning algorithms.
answer_2: An 'automated employment decision tool' is defined as any system that automatically filters candidates for hire or for any term, condition, or privilege of employment in a way that establishes a preferred candidate or candidates. This definition encompasses systems governed by statistical theory and systems whose parameters are defined by other learning algorithms, including linear regression, neural networks, decision trees, random forests, and other learning algorithms. (Definition provided in Section a. of the Act)

policy_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 11225 ("Establishment of unmanned system program and autonomous control and computer vision technology project")
question: What are the key components of the unmanned system program that the Secretary is required to establish under this section, including the types of unmanned systems to be utilized?
answer_1:
The key components of the unmanned system program that the Secretary is required to establish under this section include the use of land-based, cutter-based, and aircraft-based unmanned systems for the purpose of increasing effectiveness and efficiency of mission execution. The types of unmanned systems to be utilized are specified as:

1. Unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), as defined in section 44801 of title 49.
2. Unmanned marine surface systems.
3. Unmanned marine subsurface systems.

Citation: Title 14, United States Code, Section 319(a)
answer_2: 1) The Secretary is required to establish an unmanned system program for the use of land-based, cutter-based, and aircraft-based unmanned systems under the control of the Commandant. 2) The types of unmanned systems include unmanned aircraft systems, unmanned marine surface systems, and unmanned marine subsurface systems, as defined in the section.

policy_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 11225 ("Establishment of unmanned system program and autonomous control and computer vision technology project")
question: Beyond the retrofitting of small boats, what are the expected outcomes and data collection objectives of the Autonomous Control and Computer Vision Technology Project?
answer_1:
The Autonomous Control and Computer Vision Technology Project, as outlined in the provided context (SEC. 11225), aims to retrofit existing Coast Guard small boats with commercially available autonomous control and computer vision technology, sensors, and necessary communication systems for search and rescue, surveillance, and interdiction missions (SEC. 11225(b)(1)). The project also includes data collection and evaluation of field-collected operational data from the retrofitted boats to inform future requirements (SEC. 11225(b)(2)). The expected outcomes of the project are to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of using autonomous control and computer vision technology in Coast Guard missions. The data collection objectives are to gather operational data from the retrofitted boats to evaluate their performance and inform future requirements for unmanned systems in the Coast Guard (SEC. 11225(b)(2)).

Citation: SEC. 11225 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (NDAA 2022)
answer_2: 1) The Autonomous Control and Computer Vision Technology Project aims to retrofit existing Coast Guard small boats with commercially available autonomous control and computer vision technology, sensors, and communication methods for search and rescue, surveillance, and interdiction missions. 2) As part of the project, the Commandant is expected to collect and evaluate field-collected operational data from the retrofit to inform future requirements. 3) Upon completion of the project, the Commandant will provide a briefing to the relevant committees in Congress, including an evaluation of the data collected from the project (Sec. 11225(a)(b)(1)-(3)).

policy_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 11225 ("Establishment of unmanned system program and autonomous control and computer vision technology project")

(c)(2) of SEC. 11225 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (H.R. 4350)

3. Sustaining competition and innovation: The strategy includes a strategy to sustain competition and innovation for procurement of unmanned systems and services for the Coast Guard, including defining opportunities for new and existing technologies (3).

References:

answer_2: The required strategy for implementing unmanned systems addresses the recommendations outlined in the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's report by including steps to implement actions recommended in the report (citation: "Leveraging Unmanned Systems for Coast Guard Missions: A Strategic Imperative", published on November 12, 2020). The strategy also includes strategic goals and acquisition strategies for proposed uses and procurements of unmanned systems, a strategy to sustain competition and innovation for procurement, and an estimate of the resources necessary to accomplish the strategy (citation: SEC. 11225(c)(1-4)).

policy_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 350 ("Strategy and assessment on use of automation and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization")
question: What are the key components of the strategy outlined in subsection (a) for leveraging AI to optimize Navy shipyards?
answer_1:
1. The strategy outlined in subsection (a) of SEC. 350 aims to leverage commercial best practices used in shipyards to improve operational efficiency. (SEC. 350(a))
2. The strategy involves developing and implementing a digital platform that uses artificial intelligence to analyze data on the maintenance and condition of shipboard assets of the Navy at shipyards. (SEC. 350(a))
3. The primary purpose of this strategy is to improve the readiness of the Armed Forces, predict and diagnose issues prior to their occurrence, and lower maintenance costs. (SEC. 350(a))

Citations:
- SEC. 350(a): https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/house-bill/2500/text#toc-H61596928
answer_2: 1) The strategy involves the Secretary of the Navy, in coordination with the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program, developing and implementing a plan to use AI to analyze data on the maintenance and condition of Navy shipboard assets at shipyards. 2) The goal is to improve the readiness of the Armed Forces, predict and diagnose issues before they occur, and lower maintenance costs. 3) The strategy also includes demonstrating a digital platform that uses AI to analyze data.

policy_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 350 ("Strategy and assessment on use of automation and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization")
question: According to subsection (b), what specific areas of cost savings and efficiency gains will the Secretary of the Navy assess in relation to AI-driven predictive maintenance?
answer_1: 1) The Secretary of the Navy will assess the costs of maintenance delays on shipboard assets of the Navy (Sec. 350(b)(1)). 2) The Secretary will also evaluate potential cost savings from adopting artificial intelligence predictive maintenance technologies to determine the condition of in-service equipment and estimate when maintenance should be performed prior to failure or end of life of such equipment (Sec. 350(b)(2)).
answer_2: 1) The Secretary of the Navy will assess the costs of maintenance delays on shipboard assets, 2) The potential cost savings of adopting artificial intelligence predictive maintenance technologies, and 3) The opportunities to demonstrate commercial best practices at shipyards, including the demonstration of AI technologies for timely predictions for maintenance and planning purposes. (Source: SEC. 350. Strategy and Assessment on Use of Automation and Artificial Intelligence for Shipyard Optimization)

policy_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 350 ("Strategy and assessment on use of automation and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization")
question: In brief, what information is the Secretary of the Navy required to present to the congressional defense committees within 180 days of the Act's enactment?
answer_1:
180 days after the enactment of the Act, the Secretary of the Navy is required to provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees that includes:

1. The strategy for leveraging commercial best practices and implementing a digital platform using artificial intelligence to analyze data on the maintenance and condition of shipboard assets of the Navy at shipyards (Sec. 350(c)(1)).
2. The results of the assessment of the costs of maintenance delays on shipboard assets of the Navy and the potential cost savings of adopting artificial intelligence predictive maintenance technologies (Sec. 350(c)(2)).
3. A plan to execute any measures pursuant to the assessment (Sec. 350(c)(3)).

Source: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Sec. 350.
answer_2: 1) The strategy for leveraging commercial best practices and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization (Sec. 350(a)). 2) The results of the assessment on the costs of maintenance delays, potential cost savings of adopting AI predictive maintenance technologies, opportunities for demonstrating commercial best practices, shipyard assets suitable for near-term AI demonstrations, resources needed for accelerating demonstrations, and any policy or technical challenges (Sec. 350(b)). 3) A plan to execute any measures resulting from the assessment (Sec. 350(c)).

policy_name: EARN IT Act of 2023, Sec. 3 (National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention)
question: Explain the specific responsibilities and expected outputs of the National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention as outlined in this section.
answer_1:
The National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention, as outlined in this section, is established to develop recommended best practices for providers of interactive computer services to prevent, reduce, and respond to online sexual exploitation of children. The Commission is composed of 19 members, including federal officials and appointed members with various qualifications such as current experience in investigating online child sexual exploitation crimes, survivor or service provider for victims of online child sexual exploitation, consumer protection, civil liberties, civil rights, privacy, computer science, software engineering, and representatives from interactive computer services with different user bases.

The Commission's expected outputs include:

1. Holding meetings, hearings, and receiving evidence as necessary to carry out its purpose (Sec. 3(i)).
2. Securing information from federal departments and agencies as needed (Sec. 3(j)).
3. Developing recommended best practices for providers of interactive computer services to prevent, reduce, and respond to online child sexual exploitation (implied from Sec. 3(b)).

The Commission is expected to function for an initial period of 5 years, with vacancies filled in the same manner as the original appointment (Sec. 3(d)). The Commission's Chairperson is the Attorney General or his/her representative, and a majority of the members constitute a quorum (Sec. 3(f), (g)). The Commission may hold meetings at the call of the Chairperson (Sec. 3(h)). The Commission members serve without compensation but are allowed travel expenses (Sec. 3(k)). The Commission is exempt from the provisions of Section 1013 of title 5, United States Code (Sec. 3(l)).
answer_2: The National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention, established by this section, is tasked with developing recommended best practices for providers of interactive computer services to prevent, reduce, and respond to online child sexual exploitation (Sec. 3(b)). The Commission is composed of 19 members, including federal officials, survivors, consumer protection experts, civil liberties/civil rights experts, privacy experts, and representatives from various interactive computer services (Sec. 3(c)). The Commission is expected to hold meetings, gather information from federal agencies, and issue reports with recommended best practices (Sec. 3(i), (j)). The Commission's initial meeting should be held within 60 days of a majority of its members being appointed, and its Chairperson is the Attorney General or his/her representative (Sec. 3(e), (f)). A majority of the Commission members constitutes a quorum, but a lesser number may hold a meeting (Sec. 3(g)). The Commission may function for an indefinite period, as Section 1013 of title 5, United States Code, does not apply to it (Sec. 3(l)).

policy_name: EARN IT Act of 2023, Sec. 3 (National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention)
question: Summarize the composition of the National Commission, detailing the required expertise and representation from various sectors.
answer_1: The National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention is composed of 19 members. The Commission includes representatives from federal agencies such as the Attorney General, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. The remaining 16 members are appointed by the leaders of the Senate and House of Representatives, and they must have specific qualifications. Four members must have current experience in investigating online child sexual exploitation crimes, with two in a law enforcement capacity and two in a prosecutorial capacity (subsection c(2)(A)). Four members must be survivors of online child sexual exploitation or have current experience in providing services for victims of online child sexual exploitation in a non-governmental capacity (subsection c(2)(B)). Two members must have current experience in matters related to consumer protection, civil liberties, civil rights, or privacy, and two must have current experience in computer science or software engineering related to matters of cryptography, data security, or artificial intelligence in a non-governmental capacity (subsection c(2)(C)). Four members must currently work for an interactive computer service, representing diverse types of businesses and areas of professional expertise, with two representing larger services (with not less than 30,000,000 monthly users in the United States) and two representing smaller services (with less than 10,000,000 monthly users in the United States) (subsection c(2)(D)). The initial appointments of members to the Commission must be made within 90 days of the date of enactment of this Act (subsection d(3)). Members serve for a term of 5 years, and vacancies are filled in the same manner as the original appointment (subsection d(2)). The Attorney General or his or her representative serves as the Chairperson of the Commission (subsection f). A majority of the members of the Commission constitutes a quorum, but a lesser number of members may hold a meeting (subsection g). The Commission may hold hearings, sit and act at such times and places, take such testimony, and receive such evidence as the Commission considers appropriate (subsection i). The Commission may secure information from any Federal department or agency necessary to carry out its duties, and the head of a Federal department or agency must furnish the information upon request of the Chairperson, unless the information is subject to an active investigation or otherwise privileged or confidential (subsection j). Members serve without compensation
answer_2: The National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention consists of 19 members. It includes representatives from federal agencies such as the Attorney General, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. The remaining 16 members are appointed from various sectors, including law enforcement, prosecution, victim services, consumer protection, civil liberties, civil rights, privacy, computer science, software engineering, and diverse types of businesses with varying monthly user counts. The Commission aims to have representation from both large and small interactive computer services. Members serve for a term of 5 years.

policy_name: EARN IT Act of 2023, Sec. 3 (National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention)
question: What are the key operational procedures of the Commission, including meeting frequency, quorum requirements, and information gathering authority?
answer_1:
1. Meeting Frequency: The Commission shall meet at the call of the Chairperson (SEC. 3(h)).
2. Quorum Requirements: A majority of the members of the Commission shall constitute a quorum, but a lesser number of members may hold a meeting (SEC. 3(g)).
3. Information Gathering Authority: The Commission may secure directly from any Federal department or agency such information as the Commission considers necessary to carry out this section and section 4. Upon request of the Chairperson of the Commission for information under this authority, the head of a Federal department or agency shall furnish the information to the Commission, unless the information is subject to an active investigation or otherwise privileged or confidential (SEC. 3(i) and (j)).
answer_2: 1. The Commission is required to hold its first meeting within 60 days of a majority of its members being appointed (sec. 3(e)). 2. A majority of the members of the Commission constitutes a quorum, but a lesser number may hold a meeting (sec. 3(g)). 3. The Commission may hold meetings at the call of the Chairperson (sec. 3(h)). 4. The Commission has the authority to secure information from any Federal department or agency it deems necessary for its purposes (sec. 3(i)(1), (j)(1)). 5. The head of a Federal department or agency must furnish the requested information to the Commission, unless it is subject to an active investigation or otherwise privileged or confidential (sec. 3(j)(2)).

policy_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence")
question: What are the key steps and timelines for designing, commencing, and reporting on the AI-driven aerial refueling pilot program outlined in this section?
answer_1:
1. Design of the pilot program: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, in collaboration with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, shall design the pilot program (Sec. 346(a)(1)).
	* Coordination and consultation: In designing the pilot program, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer shall coordinate with the Commanders of the United States Transportation Command and the United States Indo-Pacific Command and seek to consult with relevant experts in the fields of artificial intelligence, logistics, aviation, and fuel management (Sec. 346(a)(2)).
2. Commencement of the pilot program: Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, in collaboration with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, shall commence the pilot program (Sec. 346(c)).
3. Report on the pilot program: Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer shall submit a report to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate on the design of the pilot program, the status of any efforts underway to commence the pilot program, and any planned future activities to be carried out under the pilot program (Sec. 346(d)).
4. Termination of the pilot program: The authority to conduct the pilot program under this section shall terminate on January 1, 2027 (Sec. 346(e)).

Sources:
- Public Law 116-92, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020, Sec. 346.
answer_2: 1. Within 90 days of the enactment of the Act, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, in collaboration with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, shall design a pilot program (Sec. 346(a)). 2. The pilot program is to commence not later than one year after the enactment of the Act (Sec. 346(c)). 3. A report on the design, status, and planned future activities of the pilot program is to be submitted to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate not later than one year after the enactment of the Act (Sec. 346(d)). 4. The authority to conduct the pilot program under this section shall terminate on January 1, 2027 (Sec. 346(e)).

policy_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence")
question: Who are the primary stakeholders responsible for the design, execution, and oversight of this AI pilot program for aerial refueling, and what are their respective roles?
answer_1:
1. The primary stakeholders responsible for the design, execution, and oversight of this AI pilot program for aerial refueling are the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense (DoD), the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force.

2. The roles of these stakeholders are as follows:
   - The Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer is responsible for designing the pilot program in collaboration with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force (Section 346(a)(1)). The Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer is also responsible for coordinating with the Commander of the United States Transportation Command and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command regarding the activities to be carried out under the pilot program (Section 346(a)(2)(A)).
   - The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment is not explicitly mentioned as having a specific role in the design of the pilot program, but is implied as a collaborator in the design process (Section 346(a)(1)).
   - The Chief of Staff of the Air Force is a collaborator in the design of the pilot program (Section 346(a)(1)).
   - The Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, in collaboration with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, is responsible for commencing the pilot program not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act (Section 346(c)).
   - The Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer is also responsible for submitting a report to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate on the design of the pilot program, the status of any efforts underway to commence the pilot program, and any planned future activities to be carried out under the pilot program (Section 346(d)).
   - The authority to conduct the pilot program under this section shall terminate on January 1, 2027 (Section 346(e)).

Citations:
- National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 346, Title III, Subtitle B, Part III,
answer_2: 1) The Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense is responsible for designing the pilot program (Sec. 346(a)(1)). 2) The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force collaborate with the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer in designing and executing the pilot program (Sec. 346(a)(1) and (c)). 3) The Commander of the United States Transportation Command and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command provide input on the activities to be carried out under the pilot program to ensure alignment with existing operational requirements (Sec. 346(a)(2)(A)). 4) Relevant experts in the fields of artificial intelligence, logistics, aviation, and fuel management are consulted during the design phase (Sec. 346(a)(2)(B)). 5) The Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer submits a report to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate regarding the pilot program's design, status, and future activities (Sec. 346(d)).

policy_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence")
question: Beyond enhancing efficiency and reducing costs, what broader strategic goals, such as improving military readiness or addressing cybersecurity concerns, does this AI pilot program intend to achieve?
answer_1:
1. Improving Military Readiness: The AI pilot program aims to enhance situational awareness and decision-making capabilities through real-time data analysis and predictive modeling, which can contribute to improving military readiness by enabling more effective and timely responses to changing operational conditions in contested logistics environments (Sec. 346(b)(4)).

2. Addressing Cybersecurity Concerns: The pilot program also seeks to evaluate potential challenges and risks associated with the integration of artificial intelligence and other advanced digital technologies, including cybersecurity concerns (Sec. 346(b)(5)). This objective highlights the importance of ensuring the security of AI systems and data in military operations.

Citation: Public Law 116-283, Section 346.
answer_2: 1) The AI pilot program aims to improve military readiness by enhancing situational awareness and decision-making capabilities through real-time data analysis and predictive modeling (Sec. 346(b)(4)). 2) It also seeks to address potential challenges and risks associated with the integration of artificial intelligence and other advanced digital technologies, including cybersecurity concerns (Sec. 346(b)(5)).

policy_name: Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Nuclear Regulatory Oversight")
question: What are the key areas of nuclear regulatory oversight that Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Advancement Act aims to improve or assess?
answer_1:
Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Advancement Act aims to improve or assess the following key areas of nuclear regulatory oversight:

1. Lessons learned from the COVID-19 public health emergency, including processes, procedures, and regulatory policies revised or temporarily suspended during the emergency, their impact on public health, safety, common defense, security, and the environment, and actions to incorporate lessons learned into the Commission's licensing and oversight activities (Sec. 123(a)).

2. Efficient, risk-informed oversight and inspections, including the use of risk-informed, performance-based procedures, expanded incorporation of information technologies, and staff training. Specific elements of oversight and inspections that may be modified by the use of technology, improved planning, and continually updated risk-informed, performance-based assessment are also assessed. Measures to improve oversight and inspections, advance risk-informed procedures, and enable licensee innovations that may advance nuclear reactor operational efficiency and safety are also identified (Sec. 123(b)).

3. A review of office and other facility space requirements of the Commission, including costs associated with the headquarters, regional offices, and technical training center, opportunities to reduce future costs, and recommendations to Congress, the Commission, and the General Services Administration for actions that may assist in reducing office and facility costs (Sec. 123(c)).

Citations:
- Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123(a)
- Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123(b)
- Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123(c)
answer_2: Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Advancement Act aims to improve and assess the nuclear regulatory oversight and inspection programs carried out by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (Commission). It does this by requiring the Commission to report on actions taken during the COVID-19 public health emergency, identify improvements to the oversight and inspections programs, and review office and facility space requirements. The Commission is also tasked with assessing specific elements of oversight and inspections, improving oversight and inspections, advancing risk-informed procedures, enabling licensee innovations, and reducing office and facility costs. (Section 123, Atomic Energy Advancement Act)

policy_name: Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Nuclear Regulatory Oversight")
question: Explain the reporting requirements mandated by Section 123 for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Comptroller General, including the timelines and recipients of these reports.
answer_1:
Section 123 of the Act mandates reporting requirements for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and the Comptroller General of the United States.

For the NRC, there are two reporting requirements:

1. The NRC is required to submit a report to the appropriate committees of Congress (the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate) within 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act. This report should identify any processes, procedures, and other regulatory policies that the NRC revised or temporarily suspended during the public health emergency described in the section, examine how any revision or temporary suspension affected the ability of the NRC to license and regulate the civilian use of radioactive materials, discuss lessons learned, list actions to incorporate the lessons, and describe when the actions will be implemented (Sec. 123(a)).

2. The NRC is also required to develop and submit a report to the same committees of Congress within one year after the date of enactment of this Act. This report should identify specific improvements to the nuclear reactor and materials oversight and inspection programs, assess specific elements of oversight and inspections that may be modified by the use of technology, improved planning, and continually updated risk-informed, performance-based assessment, identify and assess measures to improve oversight and inspections, assess measures to advance risk-informed procedures, assess the ability of the Commission to enable licensee innovations, identify recommendations resulting from the assessments, identify specific actions that the Commission will take to incorporate the recommendations, and describe when the actions will be implemented (Sec. 123(b)).

For the Comptroller General, there is one reporting requirement:

The Comptroller General is required to review office and other facility space requirements of the NRC, submit a report with recommendations to the appropriate committees of Congress within one year after the date of enactment of this Act, and the report should include an examination of the costs associated with the headquarters, regional offices, and technical training center of the NRC, current and anticipated office and facility requirements to efficiently accomplish the mission of the NRC, and recommendations to Congress, the NRC, and the General Services Administration for actions that may assist in reducing office and facility costs (Sec. 123(c)).
answer_2: Section 123 of the given context mandates the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to submit two reports to the appropriate committees of Congress. The first report, due within 180 days after the date of enactment, should detail actions taken during the COVID-19 public health emergency and identify lessons learned, actions taken, and implementation timelines (Sec. 123(a)). The second report, due within a year after the date of enactment, should propose improvements to the nuclear reactor and materials oversight and inspection programs, focusing on risk-informed, performance-based procedures, information technologies, and staff training (Sec. 123(b)). Additionally, the Comptroller General is required to review office and facility space requirements of the NRC within a year after the date of enactment and submit a report with recommendations to the same committees (Sec. 123(c)).

policy_name: Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Nuclear Regulatory Oversight")
question: Summarize the intended outcomes of the office and facility space review mandated in subsection (c) of Section 123, including the specific areas of cost examination.
answer_1:
The intended outcomes of the office and facility space review mandated in subsection (c) of Section 123 include a report from the Comptroller General of the United States that examines the costs associated with the headquarters, regional offices, and technical training center of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (Commission). The report will specifically examine costs that do not support the Commission's mission, including rent subsidies for other Federal agencies, and opportunities to reduce future costs through reduction in unnecessary office space, consolidation of offices, use of advanced information technology, or any other appropriate means. The report will also examine current and anticipated office and facility requirements to efficiently accomplish the mission of the Commission. The report will include recommendations to Congress, the Commission, and the General Services Administration for actions that may assist in reducing office and facility costs to licensees and taxpayers (Section 123(c) of the Act).

policy_name: Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Nuclear Regulatory Oversight")
question: What specific aspects of nuclear reactor and materials oversight and inspection programs are targeted for efficiency improvements through technology, risk-informed procedures, and staff training, as outlined in Section 123?
answer_1:
Section 123(b) of the provided context outlines specific aspects of nuclear reactor and materials oversight and inspection programs targeted for efficiency improvements. These aspects include:

1. Use of technology, improved planning, and continually updated risk-informed, performance-based assessment, particularly in areas such as:
   - Use of travel resources
   - Planning and preparation for inspections
   - Document collection and preparation
   - The cross-cutting issues program
   - The scope of event reporting required by licensees

2. Elimination of duplicative or unnecessary activities
3. Increased use of templates in documenting inspection results
4. Periodic training of Commission staff and leadership on the application of risk-informed criteria for:
   - Inspection planning and assessments
   - Agency decision-making processes on the application of regulations and guidance
   - The application of the Commission’s standard of reasonable assurance of adequate protection

5. Increased use of inspection approaches that balance the level of resources commensurate with safety significance
6. Increased review of the use of inspection program resources based on licensee performance
7. Expansion of modern information technology, including artificial intelligence and machine learning to risk-inform oversight and inspection decisions
8. Updating the Differing Professional Views or Opinions process to ensure any impacts on agency decisions and schedules are commensurate with the safety significance of the differing opinion
9. Enabling licensee innovations that may advance nuclear reactor operational efficiency and safety, including the criteria of the Commission for timely acceptance of licensee adoption of advanced technologies, including digital technologies

Citation: The context provided is the text of Section 123 of the SECURE Nuclear Act of 2022 (H.R. 5378).
answer_2: Section 123(b) of the provided context outlines specific aspects of nuclear reactor and materials oversight and inspection programs that are targeted for efficiency improvements. These include the use of technology for travel resources, inspection planning and assessments, document collection and preparation, cross-cutting issues program, and event reporting. Additionally, it includes improved planning, risk-informed, performance-based assessment, elimination of duplicative activities, increased use of templates, periodic training of Commission staff, expansion of modern information technology like artificial intelligence and machine learning, updating the Differing Professional Views or Opinions process, and criteria for timely acceptance of licensee adoption of advanced technologies.

policy_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 916 ("Strategic management dashboard demonstration")
question: What are the key data inputs and existing information systems that will feed the strategic management dashboard demonstration?
answer_1:
1. The strategic management dashboard demonstration will incorporate data from the elements of the strategic management plan required by section 904(d) of the National Defense Authorization Act of Fiscal Year 2008 (Public Law 110-181; 10 U.S.C. note prec. 2201).
2. It will also incorporate data from the elements of the most recent annual performance plan of the Department required by section 1115(b) of title 31, United States Code, and the most recent update on performance of the Department required by section 1116 of that title.
3. The dashboard will integrate with the framework required by subsection (c) of section 125a of title 10, United States Code, for measuring the progress of the Department toward covered elements of reform (as defined in subsection (d) of that section).
4. The dashboard will be integrated with existing information systems and databases, but the specific systems are not explicitly mentioned in the provided context.

Citations:
- National Defense Authorization Act of Fiscal Year 2008 (Public Law 110-181; 10 U.S.C. note prec. 2201)
- Title 31, United States Code, sections 1115(b) and 1116
- Title 10, United States Code, section 125a(c) and (d)
answer_2: 1) The strategic management dashboard will incorporate elements of the strategic management plan required by section 904(d) of the National Defense Authorization Act of Fiscal Year 2008 (Public Law 110-181; 10 U.S.C. note prec. 2201). 2) It will also incorporate the elements of the most recent annual performance plan of the Department required by section 1115(b) of title 31, United States Code. 3) Additionally, it will use automated data feeds from existing information systems and databases. (SEC. 916(b)(4), (5) and (SEC. 916(e))
